did_you_know.text: Did you know? The prophecy of Haggai in this chapter was delivered in the second year of King Darius, on the first day of the sixth month. Haggai addressed Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
Did you know? The people claimed that the time had not yet come to rebuild the house of the LORD, even though it remained in ruins.
Did you know? Haggai posed a pointed question to the people: How could they live in their paneled houses while the house of the LORD remained in ruins?

Did you know? Haggai describes a situation of great effort producing little result: the people sow much but harvest little; they eat but are not satisfied, drink but are not quenched, put on clothes but are not warm, and their wages disappear as though placed in a bag with holes.
Did you know? Twice in the chapter, the people are called to “consider your ways,” meaning that they should examine their situation and their conduct.
Did you know? Haggai’s practical command was to go up to the mountain, bring wood, and build the house of the LORD. Building the house is presented as a way of responding to the LORD’s will.
Did you know? According to Haggai, the heavens withheld the dew and the earth withheld its produce, resulting in a shortage throughout the land.
Did you know? Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the remnant of the people obeyed the word of the LORD and the message of Haggai, and the passage says that they feared the LORD.
Did you know? After the people responded, Haggai gave them a brief and encouraging promise from the LORD: “I am with you.”

Did you know? The LORD stirred the spirit of Zerubbabel, Joshua, and all the remnant of the people, and they came and began working on the house of the LORD of hosts. The chapter states that this happened on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of Darius.
